To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic field of an interstellar cloud core is always aligned with the symmetry axis of the core, regardless of the symmetry of the cloud.
the magnetic fields in molecular cloud cores are predominantly azimuthal, that these cores are flattened, and that they are elongated along the field lines.

(1) the magnetic field in the core is always perpendicular to the symmetry axis; (2) the magnetic field is always parallel to the symmetry axis if the core is axisymmetric; and (3) the core is never prolate if the magnetic field is parallel to the symmetry axes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of finding the shape and the magnetic field configuration of a self-gravititating, isothermal, scale-free molecular cloud, which is electrically neutral, in hydrostatic equilibrium, and permeated by a magnetic field which has an arbitrary, axisymmetric, or non-axisymmetric, configuration.
the problem of the formation of stars from molecular clouds.
the problem of the equilibrium of an interstellar cloud of molecular hydrogen, with magnetic field and self-gravitation, and with the problem of its stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a magnetic field does not prevent the formation of a cloud core, but rather it delays it.
the magnetic field does not play an important role in determining the shape of molecular clouds, and that its effect on their dynamics may be neglected.
, while magnetic fields are not able to prevent the gravitational collapse of a cloud core, they are able to delay it, to change its morphology, and to modify its final state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a cloud with a non-axisymmetric shape and a non-axisymmetric magnetic field may be in equilibrium with the same density profile and the same magnetic field strength as an axisymmetric cloud.
the shape of the core is determined by its mass-to-flux ratio, and the degree of symmetry of its magnetic field.

, in a self-consistent model of a magnetized cloud, the magnetic field is the only force that can produce non-axisymmetric structures, and the magnetic field is always aligned with the axis of symmetry of the cloud.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of a magnetic field, the shape of a cloud core is determined by a single parameter, the ratio of the gravitational energy to the rotational energy.
, when the magnetic field is weak, the density and magnetic field lines are nearly parallel, and that, when the field is strong, the density and field lines are nearly orthogonal.
, in the absence of a strong external field (i.e. a strong field that is uniform over the cloud's extent), the cloud's shape is determined by the ratio between its mass and its magnetic flux.
